counting_unit: configuration-specific source-level operation occurrence, with a separate configuration-independent source identity

scope_separation.rule: The C benchmark (RUST=0), Rust benchmark (thumbv7em-none-eabihf) and C support linked with Rust (RUST=1) are discovered and reported separately.
scope_separation.shared_c_sources: Shared C files are parsed in both C configurations. Both configuration-specific records are retained; the shared source occurrence is recognised through source_identity_key.
scope_separation.third_party: Third-party FreeRTOS, HAL, CMSIS, standard-library and startup operations are excluded from project counts. Headers are used only to resolve declarations, types and macro provenance.

configuration_specific_operation_records.definition: One row in operations.csv for one configuration. The same source occurrence active in both C configurations contributes one row per configuration.
configuration_specific_operation_records.use: Per-scope descriptive counts and configuration comparison.

source_identity_key.definition: Stable hash of language, category, source file, line, column, AST kind, expression, function and source extent where available. Build configuration is deliberately excluded.
source_identity_key.use: Recognises that an occurrence active in both C configurations is the same source occurrence without deleting either configuration-specific row.

distinct_source_identities.definition: Number of distinct source_identity_key values. The all-scope value removes configuration duplicates.
distinct_source_identities.use: Unique-source view. It is not a union of overlapping operation categories.

counting_units.prohibited_aggregation: Do not call the sum of configuration-specific rows a unique-source total. Do not sum overlapping categories and call the result a count of distinct safety-relevant actions.

macro_pointer_conversion.definition: One reported macro-expansion pointer-cast occurrence per deduplicated invocation/extent key.
macro_pointer_conversion.deduplication_key: configuration, category, source file, source line, source column, AST kind, expression, function and expansion extent start.
macro_pointer_conversion.nested_casts: Multiple CSTYLE_CAST_EXPR nodes sharing the invocation/extent start collapse into one reported occurrence. The count is not a count of every AST cast node.
macro_pointer_conversion.explicit_argument_interaction: A source-written cast in a macro argument is pointer_conversion with explicit_macro_argument provenance. Macro-body pointer casts at the same invocation are recorded in that occurrence details under collapsed_macro_pointer_conversions rather than adding a second occurrence.

provenance_classes.explicit_source: The node's spelling location equals its expansion location; the operation is written in project source.
provenance_classes.project_macro_expansion: The spelling location is a macro definition in a project header or source file. The invocation location is retained.
provenance_classes.third_party_macro_expansion: The spelling location is a macro definition outside the project source/header roots. The invocation location is retained.
provenance_classes.compiler_generated: A compiler-synthesised or unspellable AST construct with no distinct source spelling. No reported C category currently relies on this class.
provenance_classes.unresolved_provenance: Macro expansion is present but the definition or expansion origin could not be established. Pointer conversions in this class are emitted as unresolved_pointer_conversion.
provenance_classes.known_macro_model: A narrowly specified Rust addr_of!/addr_of_mut! form was modelled for a direct static-mut identifier.
provenance_classes.macro_not_expanded: A Rust macro expression retained as unresolved because the syntax-only extractor cannot expand it.
provenance_classes.explicit_macro_argument: A source-written cast whose spelling location lies inside the arguments of a macro invocation. It is counted as pointer_conversion but is not called a macro-body cast.
provenance_classes.macro_argument_reference: A non-cast source reference spelled inside a macro invocation argument. It is retained with macro_argument_* metadata; global-reference deduplication is unchanged.

pointer_dereference.c: Unary * operator whose operand has a compiler-resolved pointer type.
pointer_dereference.rust: Unary * operand whose local/parameter/static/function-return type is syntactically resolved to a raw pointer.
pointer_dereference.trigger: C: AST UNARY_OPERATOR with '*'; Rust: ExprUnary(Deref).
pointer_dereference.provenance: C explicit_source or macro-expansion classes. Macro-expanded dereferences remain pointer_dereference records with provenance metadata.
pointer_dereference.included: Explicit dereference. Rust simple aliases and direct project-function pointer returns are resolved when unambiguous.
pointer_dereference.excluded: Pointer declarations, pointer field access, array indexing, safe-reference dereference.
pointer_dereference.activity: Inactive configuration records are retained with activity_status=false and excluded from active counts.
pointer_dereference.resolution: C resolved by the compiler type. Rust resolved only when the operand type is syntactically established; otherwise the candidate remains unresolved.
pointer_dereference.overlaps: A pointer dereference may be one component of an assignment or pointer arithmetic expression.
pointer_dereference.comparable: Comparable with qualifications after mapping C -> and array-index exclusions.

pointer_field_access.c: Member expression using -> on a pointer operand.
pointer_field_access.rust: Not emitted as a separate syntax category.
pointer_field_access.trigger: C AST MEMBER_REF_EXPR containing the -> token.
pointer_field_access.included: Pointer-base member access. The pointer base is a value read.
pointer_field_access.excluded: Dot member access on an object, explicit unary dereference.
pointer_field_access.overlaps: A -> expression implies a dereference semantically but is not also emitted as pointer_dereference.
pointer_field_access.reason: Rust has no separate syntactic equivalent; descriptive only.

pointer_arithmetic.c: Binary + or - with a pointer operand; pointer += or -=; prefix or postfix ++ or -- on a pointer.
pointer_arithmetic.rust: Raw-pointer .add/.offset/.sub calls whose receiver type is resolved to a raw pointer.
pointer_arithmetic.trigger: C AST binary/compound-assignment/unary operator plus pointer operand type; Rust ExprMethodCall.
pointer_arithmetic.included: Postfix p++, p--; prefix ++p, --p; compound p += n, p -= n; binary p + n, p - n, p - q.
pointer_arithmetic.excluded: Array subscripts, ordinary integer increments and non-pointer method receivers.
pointer_arithmetic.read_write: Increment/decrement of a global pointer is also a mutable-global read/write. Compound expressions may legitimately produce more than one operation record.
pointer_arithmetic.overlaps: An increment of a global pointer produces both pointer_arithmetic and mutable_global_readwrite.
pointer_arithmetic.comparable: Descriptive with explicit mapping; C and Rust express pointer stepping differently.

array_index.c: Array subscript expression. Kept separate from pointer arithmetic.
array_index.rust: Safe Rust indexing is not counted as a raw-pointer operation.
array_index.read_write: When the selected object is a global array, an element write marks the array object as written. The index expression itself remains a read (or read/write if it is an increment).
array_index.excluded: Pointer arithmetic and Rust safe indexing.
array_index.reason: Counts different language constructs; descriptive only.

pointer_conversion.c: Explicit source-level cast with a pointer target and a pointer or integer source, written directly or as a macro invocation argument.
pointer_conversion.rust: Explicit as-cast whose target is a raw pointer.
pointer_conversion.trigger: C AST CSTYLE_CAST_EXPR whose spelling location equals its expansion location. Rust ExprCast with pointer target.
pointer_conversion.provenance: explicit_source for a direct cast; explicit_macro_argument for a cast written in a macro argument. Macro-body and third-party macro casts are excluded.
pointer_conversion.included: Explicit pointer-to-pointer and integer-to-pointer casts written in project source, including casts passed as macro arguments.
pointer_conversion.excluded: Casts generated by project or third-party macro bodies, implicit compiler conversions, unresolved-provenance casts, and pointer-to-integer casts whose target is not a pointer.
pointer_conversion.resolution: C source and target types are compiler-resolved. Conversion direction is recorded as pointer_to_pointer or integer_to_pointer.
pointer_conversion.overlaps: Nested explicit casts are counted separately. If a source-written macro-argument cast shares an invocation with macro-body pointer casts, the macro-body casts are preserved in collapsed_macro_pointer_conversions details and do not create a second occurrence.
pointer_conversion.comparable: Comparable with qualifications after documenting nested casts and the absence of a Rust integer-to-pointer distinction.

macro_pointer_conversion.c: Pointer-target cast introduced by expanding a project or third-party macro.
macro_pointer_conversion.rust: Not emitted; Rust macro contents remain unresolved unless a known addr_of! form is modelled.
macro_pointer_conversion.trigger: C AST CSTYLE_CAST_EXPR whose spelling location differs from its expansion location.
macro_pointer_conversion.provenance: project_macro_expansion or third_party_macro_expansion, with macro-definition and invocation locations.
macro_pointer_conversion.included: Pointer-target casts introduced by project or third-party macro bodies, from pointer or integer sources.
macro_pointer_conversion.excluded: Explicit source casts and source-written casts in macro arguments (pointer_conversion), non-pointer targets, and unresolved provenance.
macro_pointer_conversion.reason: Descriptive provenance category. It must not be added to pointer_conversion or presented as explicit project-written casts.
macro_pointer_conversion.counting_unit: one reported macro-expansion pointer-cast occurrence per deduplicated invocation/extent key
macro_pointer_conversion.deduplication: Multiple AST cast nodes sharing the invocation line, column and expansion extent start collapse into one record. This avoids duplicate expansion nodes but does not count every AST cast node.
macro_pointer_conversion.note: At an invocation that also contains a source-written macro-argument cast, macro-body pointer casts are retained in the explicit record collapsed_macro_pointer_conversions list, not as a separate macro_pointer_conversion row.

dynamic_allocation.c: Call to a recognised allocation API.
dynamic_allocation.rust: Call to a recognised allocation/FFI API.
dynamic_allocation.trigger: Call expression whose callee is a recognised allocator.
dynamic_allocation.included: Call sites. C: pvPortMalloc, malloc, calloc, realloc. Rust: the same recognised names through direct/FFI calls.
dynamic_allocation.excluded: Function declarations, indirect calls and runtime executions.
dynamic_allocation.overlaps: A Rust foreign allocator call may also be a kernel_api_call with callee_kind=rust_ffi_declaration.
dynamic_allocation.comparable: Comparable with qualifications as call-site counts; call layers differ.

deallocation.c: Call to a recognised release API.
deallocation.rust: Call to a recognised release/FFI API.
deallocation.trigger: Call expression whose callee is a recognised deallocator.
deallocation.included: Call sites. C: vPortFree, free. Rust: the same recognised names through direct/FFI calls.
deallocation.excluded: Function declarations, indirect calls and runtime executions.
deallocation.comparable: Comparable with qualifications as call-site counts.

mutable_global_read.c: Value read of a project-defined non-const file-scope object.
mutable_global_read.rust: Direct path read of a project-defined active static mut, not shadowed by a local or parameter.
mutable_global_read.trigger: C DECL_REF_EXPR with read usage; Rust ExprPath with read access.
mutable_global_read.read_write: An index expression used to select an array element is a read. A pointer base used to locate a pointee is a read.
mutable_global_read.included: C direct value reads, index reads, and pointer bases used to locate a pointee; Rust direct static-mut path reads and static-mut pointer-base index reads.
mutable_global_read.excluded: Address-taking, writes to the selected array element, pointee writes through pointers, const globals, aliases and atomics.
mutable_global_read.overlaps: A read may overlap a pointer dereference or an array index operation.
mutable_global_read.reason: C file-scope objects and Rust direct static-mut paths are different language models; descriptive only.

mutable_global_write.c: Direct write of a project-defined non-const file-scope object, including a direct global struct-field write or a write to an element of a global array.
mutable_global_write.rust: Direct assignment to a static-mut path, a field of a static-mut struct, or an element of a static-mut array.
mutable_global_write.trigger: C assignment lvalue analysis; Rust ExprAssign plus tagged field/index access.
mutable_global_write.included: g_count = 1; g_struct.field = value; g_array[i] = value; S_COUNT = 1; S_STRUCT.field = value; S_ARR[i] = value.
mutable_global_write.excluded: Writes through a global pointer (g_ptr->field, *g_ptr, g_ptr[i]) classify g_ptr as a read and record the pointee mutation as mutable_global_unresolved, not as a write to the pointer object. Index variables are not written merely because the array element is written.
mutable_global_write.read_write: Direct object mutation. Compound assignment and increment are read/write, not write.
mutable_global_write.reason: Descriptive only; not equivalent to Rust static-mut access.

mutable_global_readwrite.c: Compound assignment or prefix/postfix increment/decrement of a mutable global target.
mutable_global_readwrite.rust: Compound assignment to a direct static-mut path, static-mut struct field, or static-mut array element.
mutable_global_readwrite.trigger: C compound assignment or ++/-- on a direct global lvalue; Rust ExprBinary *Assign or lvalue mutation.
mutable_global_readwrite.included: g_count += 2; g_count++; ++g_count; S_COUNT += 1; S_COUNT -= 1; S_ARR[i] += 1; S_STRUCT.field += 1.
mutable_global_readwrite.excluded: Plain assignment (write) and plain value read.
mutable_global_readwrite.overlaps: Increment of a global pointer is also pointer_arithmetic.
mutable_global_readwrite.reason: Descriptive only; C and Rust models are not directly equivalent.

mutable_global_address.c: Address-taking of a project-defined mutable global or one of its fields/elements.
mutable_global_address.rust: &S, &mut S, or a directly modelled addr_of!(S)/addr_of_mut!(S) for an active static-mut identifier.
mutable_global_address.trigger: C unary &; Rust ExprReference or a recognised addr_of macro form.
mutable_global_address.excluded: Value reads and writes. addr_of! forms with non-identifier place expressions remain unresolved macros.
mutable_global_address.provenance: Rust modelled forms use known_macro_model with explicit tests; all other macro forms remain unresolved.
mutable_global_address.reason: Descriptive only; C and Rust address-taking are different constructs.

mutable_global_unresolved.c: A pointee mutation through a project-global-derived pointer (dereference, pointer member, or pointer index) whose target object cannot be identified.
mutable_global_unresolved.rust: A mutation through a static-mut pointer or a static-mut pointer index whose pointee identity cannot be established.
mutable_global_unresolved.trigger: Rust assignment through ExprUnary(Deref) or an index whose base is a static-mut pointer.
mutable_global_unresolved.included: C: *g_ptr = value; g_ptr->field = value; g_ptr[i] = value. Rust: *S_PTR = value; S_PTR[i] = value.
mutable_global_unresolved.excluded: Mutations through local pointers with no established relationship to a global object.
mutable_global_unresolved.read_write: The pointer value itself is a read; the pointee mutation is recorded as unresolved.
mutable_global_unresolved.resolution: unresolved; no whole-program alias analysis is performed.
mutable_global_unresolved.reason: Explicit uncertainty record; not a global-write count.

union_field_access.c: Member expression whose resolved field belongs to a union.
union_field_access.rust: Not supported by the syntax-only extractor; reported as unsupported when unions exist.

kernel_api_call.c: Call site whose callee matches a selected RTOS API or project-written kernel adapter/wrapper pattern, or an indirect/unresolved call.
kernel_api_call.rust: Call site matching a foreign RTOS declaration, RTOS API name, or project RTOS wrapper pattern.
kernel_api_call.counting_unit: source call site; a macro-expanded callee is recorded once at the source invocation location
kernel_api_call.included: Direct kernel calls, project wrappers, Rust foreign declarations and C indirect calls.
kernel_api_call.excluded: Wrapper-to-underlying-API equivalence and argument contract validity.
kernel_api_call.reason: Wrapper, direct RTOS and FFI calls are different layers. A matched kernel-operation count must not be formed by summing callee kinds.

unresolved_macro.c: Not applicable; C macro-expanded operations are represented with provenance classes.
unresolved_macro.rust: Macro expression that syn cannot expand and that is not a directly modelled addr_of!/addr_of_mut! form.
unresolved_macro.included: Every non-modelled macro expression, including unreachable! and addr_of! forms with non-identifier arguments.
unresolved_macro.excluded: Direct addr_of!(S)/addr_of_mut!(S) forms for an active static-mut identifier, which are modelled as mutable_global_address.
unresolved_macro.resolution: unresolved. The absence of extracted operations from a macro is never interpreted as zero operations.
unresolved_macro.reason: Unsupported/unknown coverage record, not a safety category.

unresolved_pointer_conversion.c: A relevant pointer-target cast whose macro provenance cannot be established. It is retained with resolution_status unresolved and is never counted as explicit.
unresolved_pointer_conversion.rust: Not emitted; Rust macro expressions remain unresolved_macro.
unresolved_pointer_conversion.included: Command-line macro casts and other unspellable macro expansions with a pointer target and pointer/integer source.
unresolved_pointer_conversion.resolution: unresolved; macro_definition_status is unresolved and invocation metadata is retained.
unresolved_pointer_conversion.reason: Unresolved coverage record, not a source-written operation count.

compiler_generated_pointer_conversion.c: A compiler-generated or implicit pointer-target cast node for which no explicit source spelling was found. It is retained descriptively and is never counted as explicit.
compiler_generated_pointer_conversion.trigger: C AST CSTYLE_CAST_EXPR with compiler_generated provenance.
compiler_generated_pointer_conversion.included: Compiler-generated/implicit pointer-target cast nodes that are visible to the AST but not source-written.
compiler_generated_pointer_conversion.reason: Compiler-generated construct, not a developer-written operation.

unsafe_contexts.c: not applicable as a language construct
unsafe_contexts.operation_association: Each Rust operation record carries in_unsafe_block, in_unsafe_function, in_unsafe_context, unsafe_context_ids and unsafe_context_status where mechanically determinable from source spans.
unsafe_contexts.nested_contexts: An operation inside nested unsafe blocks lists every containing unsafe-block context.
unsafe_contexts.rule: Lexical membership is not equivalent to an operation requiring unsafe. A foreign call, a safe operation placed inside an unsafe block, and a call to a safe wrapper are distinct properties. A safe wrapper is not assumed sound because its caller does not require unsafe.

macro_policy.c: C operations carry explicit_source, explicit_macro_argument, macro_argument_reference, project_macro_expansion, third_party_macro_expansion, compiler_generated or unresolved_provenance. pointer_conversion requires explicit_source or explicit_macro_argument. Macro-body casts are macro_pointer_conversion. Unresolved provenance is unresolved_pointer_conversion. Macro invocation and definition/argument locations are retained; an argument location is never labelled a macro definition.
macro_policy.rust: syn does not expand macros. All macro expressions remain unresolved_macro except a narrowly specified addr_of!/addr_of_mut!(identifier) form for an active static mut. Macro sites are reported by name, location and containing function.

mutable_global_model.c: Direct source-level global accesses only. Assignment context is applied to the object actually mutated: a direct object, a direct struct field, or an element of a global array. Index expressions, pointer bases, pointees, and address-taken objects are not marked as written. No whole-program alias analysis is performed.
mutable_global_model.rust: Direct active static-mut paths only, with explicit read/write/readwrite/address categories. Mutation through raw pointers is recorded separately as unresolved. Atomics, safe wrappers, aliases and full ownership analysis are outside the model.
mutable_global_model.comparison_warning: C mutable-global access and Rust static-mut access are not directly equivalent even where read/write labels are now correct.

deduplication: Occurrence IDs include configuration + category + source file + line + column + AST kind + expression + function + source extent where available. source_identity_key excludes configuration. Header declarations included by multiple translation units are merged. Genuinely distinct same-line operations with different columns/extents are retained.
aggregation: Per-scope category, layer and function summaries are recomputed from operation rows. Categories may overlap for the same source expression. The all-scope distinct-source count removes configuration duplicates only; it does not merge categories.

comparability.reason: Syntax categories differ across languages. None of the counts is a vulnerability count or a safety score.

resolution_status.resolved: The category and source location were established by the listed parser/compiler facts.
resolution_status.unresolved: The operation candidate is retained but a required type, target relationship or macro expansion was not established.
resolution_status.unsupported: The category is not implemented reliably and is excluded from quantitative conclusions.

known_limitations: Rust is syntax-aware, not type-checked; aliases, generics and indirect function values can remain unresolved.
Rust macros other than the restricted addr_of! forms are not expanded.
C macro-expanded operations are reported with provenance rather than expanded as separate application operations.
C does not perform alias analysis, so pointer/pointee identity is not resolved.
Layer classification is a deterministic path/scope proxy, not a function-by-function semantic classification.
Unsafe-context membership does not imply that an operation requires unsafe.
Operation counts are static source occurrences, not dynamic execution counts.
Lower operation counts are not evidence of fewer programming errors, lower risk or greater safety.
Inline Rust modules are traversed; out-of-line module declarations require their files to be in the configured file set and are otherwise reported as unsupported.
Macro-derived C counts are deduplicated expansion cast sites, not every AST cast node.
The C benchmark adapter includes unconditional bench_rust_* shims that are compiled but not demonstrated reachable from the C benchmark call path.
C columns are 1-based and Rust columns are 0-based; source traceability must use the language-specific convention.

A cast written in a macro argument that the compiler does not place in the expansion (for example an unused macro parameter) may not appear in the Clang AST and cannot be counted. This is a parser-visibility limitation, not evidence that the source text is absent.

source_column_conventions.macro_locations: Macro spelling locations and macro-definition locations are distinct. For a macro-body expansion, macro_definition_* is the spelling/definition location. For a source-written cast in a macro argument, macro_argument_* is the argument location and macro_definition_status is argument_not_definition.

nested_rust_modules.inline: Inline Item::Mod contents are traversed recursively.
nested_rust_modules.cfg: Parent and child cfg predicates are combined with logical AND. A false parent makes every descendant inactive, even when the child has no direct cfg attribute.
nested_rust_modules.identity: Function names are module-qualified (for example active_mod::inner::check). The simple name and module_path are retained separately.
nested_rust_modules.out_of_line: Out-of-line mod declarations are recorded. They are marked resolved_by_configuration only when a matching configured source file is present; otherwise they are reported as unsupported. They are never treated as empty inline modules.

source_scope_limitations.c_benchmark_bench_rust_shims: Functions whose names start with bench_rust_ are compiled unconditionally into the RUST=0 C benchmark and contribute to the c_benchmark_rtos_adapter layer, but are not demonstrated to be reachable from the C benchmark call path. Compilation is not runtime reachability; a syntactic call search is not a complete reachability analysis.
